title: Rust: peak memory writing 1,000,000 rows
dataset: 10 columns per row: integers, strings (one unique per row), floats, a date/time and a boolean; each row is generated as it is written, and the workbook is written to a file
method: examples/write_bench.rs. Each case runs in its own process; peak RSS from /usr/bin/time -l, median of three runs (all three within 0.2 MB, or 2 MB with shared strings). The first row only generates the rows, without writing them; that memory is included in every other figure.
notes: Hypaxel's memory does not grow with the row count. Shared strings grow with the number of distinct strings, here one per row.
rust_xlsxwriter's constant-memory mode stays low by writing the worksheet to a temporary file and zipping it on save; its default mode keeps the worksheet in memory.
reproduce: cargo run --release -p hypaxel --example write_bench -- hypaxel 1000000 out.xlsx   # or baseline, hypaxel-serde, hypaxel-shared, hypaxel-level6, rust_xlsxwriter, rust_xlsxwriter-constant-memory
